e7d9357d13840baf41b6c3a0a5a43cacb7209fcc.summary: Trend Micro reports that the Pawn Storm cyber-espionage campaign used a new Adobe Flash zero-day exploit, identified as CVE-2015-7645, in spear phishing emails targeting foreign affairs ministries. The report says the Flash zero-day affects at least Adobe Flash Player versions 19.0.0.185 and 19.0.0.207, and Adobe released a security bulletin and patch. Other methods included fake Outlook Web Access servers and compromised mail DNS settings for one ministry.

e7b50fe20edcbd0eaeb0db26485e1edeb347845f.summary: News report on CaddyWiper, a destructive wiper that ESET observed in Ukraine, seen on a few dozen systems at a limited number of organizations. It erases user data and partition information and spares domain controllers, which ESET says is probably a way for attackers to keep access. Symantec and ESET first saw wiper malware in February, with Trojan.Killdisk deployed before Russian forces crossed the border. CrowdStrike reported misuse of EaseUS Partition Master drivers. Other researchers named the malware DriveSlayer. CISA issued an advisory.

The post says the two are linked through shared intrusions, IOCs and TTPs. It cites Microsoft, Google, Guidepoint and Trend Micro reporting from 2024 to 2025 that SocGholish-linked access led to RansomHub deployment. It also covers Evil Corp's past ransomware, its LockBit work, and possible future sanctions and rebranding for RansomHub.

e78fa5bff9c6831544f19992cc3f1c632b7e5866.summary: Sysdig's Threat Research Team describes proxyjacking, an attack in which an attacker exploited Log4j (CVE-2021-44228) in an unpatched Apache Solr container, installed a proxyware agent, and sold the victim's IP addresses to proxyware services for profit. The report covers profit estimates, cloud billing costs, container images on DockerHub used to spread proxyware, and advice on billing alerts and detection rules.
